{"id": "9ed29b1f-9670-44fb-ade7-abd30511f28c", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_hCvvjBuYYyJWbCsyjWJ4gB", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Amazon EBS Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes\",\"context\":\"### Performance\\n\\n`io2` Block Express volumes have the following characteristics:\\n\\n* Average latency under 500 microseconds for 16KiB I/O size. Better outlier latency compared\\n to General Purpose volumes, reducing the frequency of I/Os exceeding 800 microseconds by over 10 times.\\n* Storage capacity up to 64 TiB (65,536 GiB).\\n* Provisioned IOPS up to 256,000, with an IOPS:GiB ratio of 1,000:1. Maximum IOPS can be\\n provisioned with volumes 256 GiB and larger (1,000 IOPS \u00d7 256 GiB = 256,000 IOPS).\\n\\n **Note:**\\n\\n You can achieve up to 256,000 IOPS with Nitro-based instances. On other instances, you can achieve up to 32,000 IOPS.\\n* Volume throughput up to 4,000 MiB/s. Throughput scales proportionally at a rate of 0.256\\n MiB/s per provisioned IOPS. Maximum throughput can be achieved at 16,000 IOPS or higher\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/provisioned-iops.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How do I choose the right Amazon EBS volume type for my workload?\",\"context\":\"### Compare provisioned IOPS SSD volumes\\n\\n[Provisioned IOPS SSD volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/provisioned-iops.html) include **io2** Block Express volumes and **io1** volumes. If you require more durability and a higher IOPS-to-GiB ratio, then use **io2** Block Express.\\n\\n**Note:** All **io2** volumes created after November 21, 2023, are **io2** Block Express volumes. To convert **io2** volumes created before November 21, 2023, to **io2** Block Express volumes, [modify the IOPS or size of the volume](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modify-volume.html).\\n\\n**Important:** If you created your **io1** volume before December 6, 2017, then you must upgrade the volume to io2 Block Express. Make sure that you provisioned 64,000 IOPS to reach the maximum 1,000 MB/s throughput.\\n\\nThe maximum values for IOPS, throughput, and latency are based on an I/O size of 16 KiB. A larger I/O size can't reach these maximum values.\\n\\nUse the following specifications to determine whether **io1** or **io2** Block Express meets your performance and durability requirements:\\n\\n| Specification | io1 | io2 Block Express |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| **Volume size** | 4 GB \u2013 16 TB | 4 GB \u2013 64 TB |\\n| **Max IOPS/volume** | 64,000 | 256,000 |\\n| **Max throughput/volume** | 1,000 MB/s | 4,000 MB/s |\\n| **Max IOPS/GB** | 50 IOPS/GB | 1,000 IOPS/GB |\\n| **Durability** | 99.8% \u2013 99.9% | 99.999% |\\n| **Multi-Attach support** | Supported | Supported |\\n| **Boot volume** | Supported | Supported |\\n| **Latency** | Single-digit millisecond | Sub-millisecond (average under 500 microseconds for 16 KiB I/O) |\\n| **Instance availability** | All EC2 instances | All EC2 instances built on the [AWS Nitro System](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/nitro/) |\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ebs-volume-type-differences\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"How do I calculate the maximum IOPS and throughput for an Amazon EBS volume?\",\"context\":\"Resolution\\n----------\\n\\nWhen an Amazon EBS volume reaches reaches its IOPS or throughput quota, it can experience high latency. To troubleshoot latency issues on an EBS volume, calculate the maximum available IOPS and throughput quota.\\n\\nThe available IOPS and throughput for an EBS volume can vary depending on volume type, volume size, and provisioned IOPS.\\n\\nTo find the maximum available IOPS and throughput for your EBS volume, use the following interactive bash script. Then, analyze the performance of your EBS volume based on the quotas. For more information, see [VolumeLimitCalculator](https://github.com/awslabs/aws-support-tools/tree/master/EBS/VolumeLimitCalculator) on the GitHub website.\\n\\nComplete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Download the **VolumeLimitCalculator** script to your Linux instance, and convert it to a format that you can run:\\n ```plaintext\\n # chmod +x volume_Limit_calculator.sh\\n ```\\n \\n2. Run the script:\\n ```plaintext\\n # ./volume_Limit_calculator.sh\\n ```\\n **Note:** The preceding script doesn't calculate IOPS and throughput for io2 block express volumes.\\n\\nRelated information\\n-------------------\\n\\n[Amazon EBS volume types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-volume-types.html)\\n\\n[How do I optimize the performance of my Amazon EBS volumes?](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ebs-performance)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ebs-maximum-iops-throughput\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up EBS io2 IOPS quota documentation"}

{"id": "457fed00-e86a-4c8f-94bc-e929465103aa", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You've hit the regional io2 IOPS quota, which is an adjustable limit. You can ask for an increase.

**What's happening**
- The quota is "IOPS for Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volumes" (code `L-8D977E7E`). It's the total provisioned IOPS across all io2 volumes in a region, not a per-volume limit.
- In us-east-1 in this account (012345678901_1), the value is currently **100,000**. Your 150K request is above that on its own. Any io2 volumes you already have count toward the total, so you need headroom for them too.

**What to do**
1. **Request a quota increase.** Raise the quota to at least 150,000 plus the IOPS your existing io2 volumes use. A bit of extra headroom saves you from repeating this.
   - Use the Service Quotas console, or the `request-service-quota-increase` CLI command with service code `ebs` and quota code `L-8D977E7E`.
   - Make the request in the same region where the volume creation failed. Quotas are per region, and I checked us-east-1.
2. **Check your related storage quota.** The io2 storage quota (`L-09BD8365`) is 20 TiB. A 150K IOPS volume needs at least 150 GiB at the 1,000:1 IOPS:GiB ratio, so you're probably fine. If you plan to provision a lot of io2 capacity, raise it in the same request.
3. **Confirm the instance supports it.** io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS per volume. You only get more than 32,000 IOPS on Nitro-based instances. On other instance types you'd be capped at 32,000 IOPS even with a higher quota.
4. **In the meantime, reduce the request.** If you need the volume now, provision it at or below the remaining quota. You can raise the IOPS later with `modify-volume` once the increase is approved.

If you give me the region and the target IOPS total, I can submit the increase request for you. You'd need to approve it before it runs. I can also add up the IOPS your existing io2 volumes use so we can size the request properly.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
